title: Extension of derived descent solutions across two open unions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal B$ be a set of open subsets covering $X$, with $U\cap V=\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal B,\,T\subset U\cap V}T$ for $U,V\in\mathcal B$. For every $U\in\mathcal B$ give $K_U\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pc-derived-category] and for every inclusion $V\subset U$ in $\mathcal B$ give an isomorphism $\rho_V^U:K_U|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}K_V$, with $\rho_U^U=1$ and $\rho_T^U=\rho_T^V\circ(\rho_V^U|_T)$ for $T\subset V\subset U$. Assume $\operatorname{Hom}(K_U,K_U[i])=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and every integer $i<0$. For a union $O$ of members of $\mathcal B$, put $\mathcal B_O=\{U\in\mathcal B:U\subset O\}$. A solution on $O$ means an object $F\in D(\mathcal O_O)$ with isomorphisms $s_U:F|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}K_U$ for every $U\in\mathcal B_O$, satisfying $\rho_V^U\circ(s_U|_V)=s_V$ for all inclusions $V\subset U$ in $\mathcal B_O$. Let $O_1,O_2$ be unions of members of $\mathcal B$ with supplied solutions $(F_1,s_1)$ and $(F_2,s_2)$. There is a unique isomorphism $c_{12}:F_1|_{O_1\cap O_2}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2|_{O_1\cap O_2}$ with $s_{2,V}\circ(c_{12}|_V)=s_{1,V}$ for every $V\in\mathcal B_{O_1\cap O_2}$. For any third union $O_3$ with a supplied solution, the similarly characterized comparisons satisfy $c_{13}=c_{23}\circ c_{12}$ on $O_1\cap O_2\cap O_3$. There exist a solution $(F,s)$ on $O_1\cup O_2$ and isomorphisms $f_j:F|_{O_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_j$ for $j=1,2$ such that $f_2|_{O_1\cap O_2}=c_{12}\circ(f_1|_{O_1\cap O_2})$ and $s_U=s_{j,U}\circ(f_j|_U)$ whenever $U\in\mathcal B_{O_j}$. The solution supplies $s_U$ and its inclusion equations for every $U\in\mathcal B_{O_1\cup O_2}$, including those contained in neither $O_1$ nor $O_2$. No quasi-compactness or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Put $O=O_1\cup O_2$ and $W=O_1\cap O_2$. Every finite intersection of unions of $\mathcal B$ is again a union of $\mathcal B$: for a point in the intersection choose a containing member in each union and repeatedly use the intersection-refinement hypothesis. Consequently $\mathcal B_W$ covers $W$, and any two of its members have their intersection covered by smaller members of $\mathcal B_W$. The same holds for a triple intersection and for every union considered below. We regard each such open as its open subscheme.

source.place: Tag 0D69 (cohomology-remark-uniqueness), restriction of the intersection-refining family

proof.text: On $V\in\mathcal B_W$ set $a_V=s_{2,V}^{-1}\circ s_{1,V}$. The solution equations give $a_U|_V=s_{2,V}^{-1}(\rho_V^U)(\rho_V^U)^{-1}s_{1,V}=a_V$ when $V\subset U$. For each of the four ordered pairs of objects among $F_1|_W,F_2|_W$, their restrictions to $V$ are isomorphic to $K_V$, so their negative Hom groups vanish by conjugating with the supplied isomorphisms. Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] on $W$ with family $\mathcal B_W$. It glues $(a_V)$ to a unique map $c_{12}$ and $(a_V^{-1})$ to a map in the reverse direction. Injectivity in that same result for both endomorphism pairs shows their composites are identities, since their restrictions to every $V$ are identities. Thus $c_{12}$ is the required unique isomorphism.

For three solutions repeat step 2 on their pairwise intersections. On each $V\in\mathcal B$ contained in the triple intersection, the restrictions of $c_{23}c_{12}$ and $c_{13}$ are both $s_{3,V}^{-1}s_{1,V}$. Apply injectivity in [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] on that intersection for the pair $F_1,F_3$, whose local negative Hom vanishes by their identifications with $K_V$. This proves the asserted cocycle equation.

Apply [lem-sc-derived-open-gluing-objects] to the scheme $O$, its two opens $O_1,O_2$, and the objects $F_1,F_2$ with overlap isomorphism $c_{12}$. It gives $F\in D(\mathcal O_O)$ and isomorphisms $f_j:F|_{O_j}\to F_j$ satisfying $f_2|_W=c_{12}(f_1|_W)$. Its conclusion uses the canonical iterated-restriction comparisons; we use those same comparisons in all following restriction equations.

Fix any $U\in\mathcal B_O$, including a member crossing both pieces. Let $\mathcal C_U=\{V\in\mathcal B:V\subset U,\ V\subset O_1\text{ or }V\subset O_2\}$. It covers $U$: choose a member $A$ contained in a piece and containing the point, then refine $A\cap U$. It is intersection-refining because a smaller member of the intersection remains in a piece. For $V\in\mathcal C_U$ define $\tau_V=s_{j,V}(f_j|_V)$ using a piece containing $V$. If both pieces contain $V$, step 2 and step 4 give $s_{2,V}(f_2|_V)=s_{2,V}(c_{12}|_V)(f_1|_V)=s_{1,V}(f_1|_V)$, so the definition is independent of $j$. For $T\subset V$ in $\mathcal C_U$ choose the same piece as for $V$; then $\rho_T^V(\tau_V|_T)=\tau_T$. Define $b_V=(\rho_V^U)^{-1}\tau_V:F|_V\to K_U|_V$. The cocycle equation for $\rho$ gives $b_V|_T=(\rho_T^U)^{-1}\tau_T=b_T$. All $b_V$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0D6A (cohomology-lemma-solution-in-finite-case), two-open case: the family B-prime and its two solutions

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] on $U$ with family $\mathcal C_U$ and pair $F|_U,K_U$. On $V\in\mathcal C_U$ both objects are isomorphic to $K_V$, through $\tau_V$ and $\rho_V^U$, so its negative-Hom hypothesis holds. The compatible $b_V$ glue uniquely to $s_U:F|_U\to K_U$. Apply the same result in the reverse direction to $b_V^{-1}$, and for each endomorphism pair to compare the two composites with the identity. All these pairs have local negative Hom zero by the same identifications with $K_V$. Injectivity therefore shows that $s_U$ is an isomorphism, with $\rho_V^U(s_U|_V)=\tau_V$ for every $V\in\mathcal C_U$. This construction applies to every $U\in\mathcal B_O$.

source.place: Tags 0D68 and 0D6A (cohomology-lemma-solution-in-finite-case), unique comparison of the two solutions on U

proof.text: If $U\subset O_j$, the map $s_{j,U}(f_j|_U)$ has the same restrictions $b_V$ as $s_U$ on $\mathcal C_U$, by the solution equations. Injectivity in [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] for $F|_U,K_U$ gives their equality. For an arbitrary inclusion $T\subset U$ in $\mathcal B_O$, every $V\in\mathcal C_T$ also lies in $\mathcal C_U$. Thus $\rho_V^T((\rho_T^U(s_U|_T))|_V)=\rho_V^U(s_U|_V)=\tau_V=\rho_V^T(s_T|_V)$. Cancel $\rho_V^T$ and use injectivity for the pair $F|_T,K_T$ on $\mathcal C_T$ to conclude $\rho_T^U(s_U|_T)=s_T$. Its local negative Hom hypothesis again follows from $\tau_V,\rho_V^T$. Hence all structure maps, including the crossing ones, satisfy the required equations. Empty opens or an empty family on the empty scheme are included by the empty-cover clause of the Hom-gluing lemma and the unrestricted two-open gluing assertion; no finite subcover or cohomological bound was used.
